```{r}
#| label: setup

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# HOW TO READ THIS FILE
#
# Most of this is code you have already written in class:
#   get_acs() (Week 9), filter / mutate / group_by / summarize / pivot_wider
#   (Weeks 2-3), joins (Week 3), ggplot2 (Weeks 4-7), st_as_sf() / st_join() /
#   scale bars (Week 10, HW4), and the dashboard layout itself (Week 8:
#   "# Page", "## Row", "### Column", and one card per code chunk).
#
# Four things are new. Each one is marked "NEW:" where it shows up:
#   1. Value boxes (the colored number tiles): a ::: {.valuebox} block
#   2. The interactive map: the long version of mapgl's maplibre_view()
#   3. The searchable table: reactable(), which needs
#      install.packages("reactable") once
#   4. dashboard.scss: optional styling. You can ignore it entirely.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

library(tidyverse)
library(tidycensus)
library(sf)
library(tigris)
library(ggspatial)
library(mapgl)
library(reactable)

options(tigris_use_cache = TRUE)

# One theme for every static figure, so the pages look like one product
theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 14))

# One color per idea, used on every page:
# purple = older residents, orange = nursing homes, grey = U.S. benchmark
age_purple  <- "#54278F"
home_orange <- "#B04E0A"
```

```{r}
#| label: data-census

# ---- 1. Which counties are in the NBRC region? ----------------------------
# The same 63-county list we used in Week 9 (it lives in the site's data/ folder)
nbrc_counties <- read_csv("../data/nbrc_counties_fips.csv",
                          col_types = cols(.default = "c"))

nbrc_states <- c("ME", "NH", "NY", "VT")

# ---- 2. Age data from the ACS ---------------------------------------------
# Table B01001 is "Sex by Age." Line 001 is total population.
# Lines 020-025 are men 65 and older; lines 044-049 are women 65 and older.
age_vars <- c(total = "B01001_001",
              "B01001_020", "B01001_021", "B01001_022",   # men 65+
              "B01001_023", "B01001_024", "B01001_025",
              "B01001_044", "B01001_045", "B01001_046",   # women 65+
              "B01001_047", "B01001_048", "B01001_049")

# Four pulls: NBRC-state counties and the whole U.S., in two time periods.
# mutate(year = ...) labels each one so we can stack them.
acs_county_2024 <- get_acs(geography = "county", state = nbrc_states,
                           variables = age_vars, year = 2024) |>
  mutate(year = 2024)

acs_county_2019 <- get_acs(geography = "county", state = nbrc_states,
                           variables = age_vars, year = 2019) |>
  mutate(year = 2019)

acs_us_2024 <- get_acs(geography = "us", variables = age_vars, year = 2024) |>
  mutate(year = 2024)

acs_us_2019 <- get_acs(geography = "us", variables = age_vars, year = 2019) |>
  mutate(year = 2019)

# Stack all four (bind_rows), then add up the twelve 65+ lines.
# Result: one row per place per year, with columns pop and pop65.
age_by_place <- bind_rows(acs_county_2024, acs_county_2019,
                          acs_us_2024, acs_us_2019) |>
  mutate(group = if_else(variable == "total", "pop", "pop65")) |>
  group_by(GEOID, year, group) |>
  summarize(estimate = sum(estimate), .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = group, values_from = estimate) |>
  mutate(share65 = pop65 / pop)

# ---- 3. Regional totals ---------------------------------------------------
# Add up the counts across counties first, THEN divide.
# (Averaging 63 county percentages would treat Hamilton County, NY,
# with about 5,000 people, the same as Saratoga County, NY, with about 240,000.)
nbrc_by_year <- age_by_place |>
  filter(GEOID %in% nbrc_counties$full_fips) |>
  group_by(year) |>
  summarize(pop = sum(pop), pop65 = sum(pop65)) |>
  mutate(share65 = pop65 / pop)

us_by_year <- age_by_place |>
  filter(GEOID == "1")          # the U.S. has GEOID "1"

nbrc_share_2024 <- nbrc_by_year |> filter(year == 2024) |> pull(share65)
nbrc_share_2019 <- nbrc_by_year |> filter(year == 2019) |> pull(share65)
us_share_2024   <- us_by_year |> filter(year == 2024) |> pull(share65)
us_share_2019   <- us_by_year |> filter(year == 2019) |> pull(share65)
us_pop65_2024   <- us_by_year |> filter(year == 2024) |> pull(pop65)

# ---- 4. One row per county, both periods side by side ---------------------
# pivot_wider() turns the two years into columns: share65_2019, share65_2024...
county_stats <- age_by_place |>
  filter(GEOID %in% nbrc_counties$full_fips) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = year, values_from = c(pop, pop65, share65)) |>
  mutate(change = share65_2024 - share65_2019) |>
  left_join(nbrc_counties |> select(GEOID = full_fips, state, county_name),
            by = "GEOID") |>
  mutate(label = paste0(county_name, ", ", state))     # "Essex, VT"

n_above_us <- sum(county_stats$share65_2024 > us_share_2024)

# County shapes from TIGER (cartographic boundary files, cb = TRUE)
county_shapes <- counties(state = nbrc_states, cb = TRUE, year = 2024,
                          progress_bar = FALSE) |>
  filter(GEOID %in% nbrc_counties$full_fips) |>
  select(GEOID)
```

```{r}
#| label: data-nursing-homes

# ---- 5. Nursing homes from CMS --------------------------------------------
# CMS "Provider Information" file: one row per Medicare/Medicaid-certified
# nursing home in the country, with coordinates, beds, and star ratings.
# https://data.cms.gov/provider-data/dataset/4pq5-n9py
# The download link changes every month, so we saved a dated copy.
homes_raw <- read_csv("data/NH_ProviderInfo_Oct2026.csv",
                      show_col_types = FALSE)

# Keep the 50 states + DC, keep the columns we use, give them short names.
# (Backticks let us refer to column names that have spaces in them.)
homes_us <- homes_raw |>
  filter(State %in% c(state.abb, "DC")) |>
  select(name      = `Provider Name`,
         town      = `City/Town`,
         state     = State,
         beds      = `Number of Certified Beds`,
         residents = `Average Number of Residents per Day`,
         stars     = `Overall Rating`,
         ownership = `Ownership Type`,
         turnover  = `Total nursing staff turnover`,
         staff_hrs = `Reported Total Nurse Staffing Hours per Resident per Day`,
         lon = Longitude, lat = Latitude) |>
  mutate(name = str_to_title(name), town = str_to_title(town))

# Points: st_as_sf() turns the lon/lat columns into geometry (as in HW4).
# Then match the county shapes' CRS before any spatial operation (Week 10).
homes_sf <- homes_us |>
  st_as_sf(coords = c("lon", "lat"), crs = 4326) |>
  st_transform(st_crs(county_shapes))

# Spatial join: which NBRC county is each home in?
# left = FALSE drops every home that isn't inside an NBRC county.
nbrc_homes <- homes_sf |>
  st_join(county_shapes, left = FALSE)

# Count homes and beds per county...
county_beds <- nbrc_homes |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  group_by(GEOID) |>
  summarize(homes = n(), beds = sum(beds, na.rm = TRUE))

# ...and join to the county table. Counties with no homes get NA from the
# join, so replace_na() turns those into 0.
county_stats <- county_stats |>
  left_join(county_beds, by = "GEOID") |>
  mutate(homes = replace_na(homes, 0),
         beds  = replace_na(beds, 0),
         beds_per_1k = beds / pop65_2024 * 1000)

# ---- 6. Benchmarks for the value boxes and text ---------------------------
nbrc_beds_per_1k <- sum(county_stats$beds) / sum(county_stats$pop65_2024) * 1000
us_beds_per_1k   <- sum(homes_us$beds, na.rm = TRUE) / us_pop65_2024 * 1000

n_no_home <- sum(county_stats$homes == 0)

nbrc_turnover <- median(nbrc_homes$turnover, na.rm = TRUE)
us_turnover   <- median(homes_us$turnover, na.rm = TRUE)
nbrc_staff    <- median(nbrc_homes$staff_hrs, na.rm = TRUE)
us_staff      <- median(homes_us$staff_hrs, na.rm = TRUE)

# Share of rated homes with one star. mean() of TRUE/FALSE = share TRUE.
nbrc_one_star <- mean(nbrc_homes$stars == 1, na.rm = TRUE)
us_one_star   <- mean(homes_us$stars == 1, na.rm = TRUE)

# Do older counties have fewer beds per senior? (cor() from Week 4)
age_beds_cor <- cor(county_stats$share65_2024, county_stats$beds_per_1k)

# Counties as an sf object for the maps
county_map <- county_shapes |>
  left_join(county_stats, by = "GEOID")
```

```{r}
#| label: numbers-for-text

# Every number that appears in the value boxes and the text, formatted once.
# Then the text below just says `{r} txt_share_nbrc` and so on.
txt_share_nbrc <- scales::percent(nbrc_share_2024, accuracy = 0.1)
txt_share_us   <- scales::percent(us_share_2024, accuracy = 0.1)

# Change in percentage points. "\u00a0" is a non-breaking space: a value box
# number with a plain space in it doesn't display correctly.
txt_change_nbrc <- paste0("+", round(100 * (nbrc_share_2024 - nbrc_share_2019), 1), "\u00a0pts")
txt_change_us   <- paste0("+", round(100 * (us_share_2024 - us_share_2019), 1), "\u00a0pts")

txt_homes <- nrow(nbrc_homes)
txt_beds  <- scales::comma(sum(nbrc_homes$beds, na.rm = TRUE))

txt_beds_1k_nbrc <- round(nbrc_beds_per_1k, 1)
txt_beds_1k_us   <- round(us_beds_per_1k, 1)

txt_turnover_nbrc <- paste0(round(nbrc_turnover, 1), "%")
txt_turnover_us   <- paste0(round(us_turnover, 1), "%")
txt_one_star_nbrc <- scales::percent(nbrc_one_star, accuracy = 1)
txt_one_star_us   <- scales::percent(us_one_star, accuracy = 1)
txt_staff_nbrc    <- round(nbrc_staff, 2)
txt_staff_us      <- round(us_staff, 2)
```

## Row {height="78%"}

### Column {width="70%"}

```{r}
#| label: map-overview
#| title: "Share of residents 65+ by county, with nursing homes (circle area = beds)"

# NEW: the long version of mapgl. In Week 10 we used the one-line version,
#   maplibre_view(county_map, column = "share65_2024")
# The long version lets us stack two layers (counties + homes) and control
# colors, sizes, legends, and what pops up when you click.

# mapgl wants longitude/latitude (EPSG 4326)
county_layer <- county_map |>
  st_transform(4326) |>
  mutate(popup = paste0("<strong>", label, "</strong><br>",
                        "Residents 65+: ", round(100 * share65_2024, 1), "%<br>",
                        "Nursing homes: ", homes, "<br>",
                        "Beds per 1,000 residents 65+: ", round(beds_per_1k, 1)))

# Circle AREA should match beds, so the radius grows with the square root.
# (Same reason scale_size_area() exists in ggplot2.)
home_layer <- nbrc_homes |>
  st_transform(4326) |>
  mutate(radius = sqrt(beds) * 0.9,
         rating = if_else(is.na(stars), "not rated", paste0(stars, " of 5 stars")),
         staff_turnover = if_else(is.na(turnover), "not reported", paste0(turnover, "%")),
         popup = paste0("<strong>", name, "</strong><br>",
                        town, ", ", state, "<br>",
                        "Certified beds: ", beds, "<br>",
                        "CMS rating: ", rating, "<br>",
                        "Nursing staff turnover: ", staff_turnover))

purples <- RColorBrewer::brewer.pal(5, "Purples")
share_breaks <- c(0.15, 0.19, 0.23, 0.27, 0.31)
legend_beds  <- c(50, 150, 300)

maplibre(style = carto_style("positron"), bounds = county_layer) |>
  # Layer 1: counties, colored by share 65+
  add_fill_layer(id = "Counties",
                 source = county_layer,
                 fill_color = interpolate(column = "share65_2024",
                                          values = share_breaks,
                                          stops = purples),
                 fill_opacity = 0.75,
                 fill_outline_color = "white",
                 tooltip = "label",          # shows on hover
                 popup = "popup") |>         # shows on click
  # Layer 2: nursing homes, sized by beds
  add_circle_layer(id = "Nursing homes",
                   source = home_layer,
                   circle_color = home_orange,
                   circle_radius = get_column("radius"),
                   circle_opacity = 0.8,
                   circle_stroke_color = "white",
                   circle_stroke_width = 1,
                   tooltip = "name",
                   popup = "popup") |>
  # Legends, and the buttons around the edge of the map
  add_legend("Residents 65+",
             values = scales::percent(share_breaks, accuracy = 1),
             colors = purples, type = "continuous",
             position = "bottom-left", width = "250px") |>
  add_legend("Certified beds",
             values = legend_beds, colors = home_orange,
             sizes = 2 * sqrt(legend_beds) * 0.9,
             type = "categorical", circular_patches = TRUE,
             position = "bottom-right", margin_bottom = 30, add = TRUE) |>
  add_layers_control(position = "top-right", collapsible = FALSE) |>
  add_navigation_control(position = "top-left") |>
  add_fullscreen_control(position = "top-left")
```

### Column {width="30%"}

::: {.card .bottom-line title="Bottom line"}
**The Northern Border region is older than the country and getting older faster. The oldest counties tend to have the fewest nursing home beds per senior.**

**Older.** `{r} txt_share_nbrc` of the region's residents are 65 or older, compared with `{r} txt_share_us` nationally. `{r} n_above_us` of the 63 NBRC counties are above the national share.

**Aging faster.** Since 2015–2019, the region's 65+ share rose `{r} round(100 * (nbrc_share_2024 - nbrc_share_2019), 1)` points, against `{r} round(100 * (us_share_2024 - us_share_2019), 1)` points for the U.S.

**Care is thinnest where need is highest.** Counties with a larger 65+ share have fewer nursing home beds per 1,000 seniors (correlation of `{r} round(age_beds_cor, 2)`). `{r} n_no_home` counties have no certified nursing home at all.

**How to use this map.** Hover over a county or a circle for its name and click for details. Use the box in the top right to turn the nursing homes off.
:::

```{r}
#| label: map-change
#| title: "Every NBRC county got older between 2015–2019 and 2020–2024"

ggplot(county_map) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = change), color = "white", linewidth = 0.3) +
  # scale = 100 turns 0.023 into 2.3; prefix adds the plus sign
  scale_fill_distiller(palette = "Purples", direction = 1,
                       labels = scales::label_number(scale = 100, prefix = "+",
                                                     accuracy = 1),
                       name = "Change in 65+ share (percentage points)") +
  annotation_scale(location = "br", unit_category = "imperial",
                   width_hint = 0.25) +
  labs(caption = "Source: ACS 5-year estimates, 2015–2019 and 2020–2024, table B01001") +
  theme_void(base_size = 14) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom",
        legend.title.position = "top",
        legend.key.width = unit(2.5, "cm"),
        plot.caption = element_text(color = "grey40", hjust = 0))
```

```{r}
#| label: dumbbell
#| title: "The 15 oldest counties, then and now"

# Same dumbbell recipe as Week 7: long data, a grey geom_line() joining
# each county's two points, then geom_point() on top.
oldest_15 <- county_stats |>
  slice_max(share65_2024, n = 15) |>
  select(label, share65_2019, share65_2024) |>
  pivot_longer(c(share65_2019, share65_2024),
               names_to = "period", values_to = "share65") |>
  mutate(period = if_else(period == "share65_2019", "2015–2019", "2020–2024"))

ggplot(oldest_15, aes(x = share65, y = fct_reorder(label, share65), color = period)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = us_share_2024, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50") +
  geom_line(aes(group = label), color = "grey70", linewidth = 1.5) +
  geom_point(size = 3.5) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("2015–2019" = "grey60", "2020–2024" = age_purple)) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::label_percent(accuracy = 1),
                     limits = c(0.15, NA)) +
  labs(x = "Share of residents 65+", y = NULL, color = NULL,
       caption = paste0("Dashed line: the U.S. in 2020–2024 (", txt_share_us, ")")) +
  theme(legend.position = "top",
        panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
        plot.caption = element_text(color = "grey40", hjust = 0))
```

```{r}
#| label: scatter
#| title: "Older counties have fewer nursing home beds per senior"

# Label a handful of counties so readers can find their bearings:
# the oldest, the youngest, the most beds per senior, and the largest county
# with no nursing home. hjust keeps the labels at the edges inside the plot.
label_these <- county_stats |>
  filter(share65_2024 == max(share65_2024) |
           share65_2024 == min(share65_2024) |
           beds_per_1k == max(beds_per_1k) |
           (homes == 0 & pop65_2024 == max(pop65_2024[homes == 0]))) |>
  mutate(hjust = case_when(share65_2024 == max(share65_2024) ~ 1,
                           share65_2024 == min(share65_2024) ~ 0,
                           .default = 0.5))

ggplot(county_stats, aes(x = share65_2024, y = beds_per_1k)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = nbrc_beds_per_1k, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50") +
  annotate("text", x = 0.335, y = nbrc_beds_per_1k, vjust = -0.5, hjust = 1,
           label = "NBRC region overall", color = "grey40", size = 3.8) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, color = "grey60", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(aes(size = pop65_2024), color = age_purple, alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_text(data = label_these, aes(label = label, hjust = hjust),
            vjust = -1.2, size = 3.6, color = "grey20") +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::label_percent(accuracy = 1)) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.05, 0.12))) +
  scale_size_area(max_size = 9, labels = scales::label_comma(),
                  name = "Residents 65+") +
  labs(x = "Share of residents 65+ (2020–2024)",
       y = "Certified beds per 1,000 residents 65+",
       caption = "Each circle is one NBRC county. Grey line: linear trend.") +
  theme(plot.caption = element_text(color = "grey40", hjust = 0))
```

```{r}
#| label: stars
#| title: "NBRC nursing homes skew toward lower CMS star ratings"

# Stack the NBRC homes and all U.S. homes, then count homes by star rating
star_shares <- bind_rows(
  nbrc_homes |> st_drop_geometry() |> mutate(group = "NBRC region"),
  homes_us |> mutate(group = "United States")
) |>
  filter(!is.na(stars)) |>
  count(group, stars) |>
  group_by(group) |>
  mutate(share = n / sum(n)) |>
  ungroup()

# position = "dodge" puts the bars side by side (Week 7); the labels need
# position_dodge() with the same width so they land on top of their bars
ggplot(star_shares, aes(x = factor(stars), y = share, fill = group)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge") +
  geom_text(aes(label = scales::percent(share, accuracy = 1)),
            position = position_dodge(width = 0.9),
            vjust = -0.4, size = 3.6) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("NBRC region" = home_orange,
                               "United States" = "grey65")) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_percent(accuracy = 1),
                     expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.1))) +
  labs(x = "CMS overall rating (stars)", y = "Share of rated homes", fill = NULL,
       caption = "Source: CMS Nursing Home Provider Information, October 2026") +
  theme(legend.position = "top",
        panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
        plot.caption = element_text(color = "grey40", hjust = 0))
```

# Data & Methods

## Row

### Column {width="65%"}

```{r}
#| label: table
#| title: "Every certified nursing home in NBRC counties (search, sort, or filter)"

home_table <- nbrc_homes |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  mutate(stars = if_else(is.na(stars), "not rated", strrep("★", stars))) |>
  select(Name = name, Town = town, State = state, Beds = beds,
         `Avg. residents` = residents, Rating = stars,
         `Staff turnover (%)` = turnover, Ownership = ownership) |>
  arrange(State, Town)

# NEW: reactable() turns a data frame into a searchable, sortable table
reactable(home_table,
          searchable = TRUE, filterable = TRUE, striped = TRUE,
          highlight = TRUE, compact = TRUE, defaultPageSize = 15,
          columns = list(
            Name = colDef(minWidth = 200),
            `Avg. residents` = colDef(format = colFormat(digits = 0)),
            Ownership = colDef(minWidth = 160)
          ))
```

### Column {width="35%"}

::: {.card title="Sources and methods"}
**Population.** American Community Survey 5-year estimates (2015–2019 and 2020–2024), table B01001 (Sex by Age), pulled with `tidycensus`. "65+" adds up the twelve age-and-sex lines for 65 and older. Regional shares add up counts across counties first and then divide, rather than averaging county percentages.

**Nursing homes.** CMS Nursing Home Provider Information, October 2026 release. It covers Medicare- and Medicaid-certified nursing homes only, so assisted living and residential care are not in these counts. Each home was placed in a county with a spatial join (`st_join()`) on its CMS coordinates. One Amsterdam, NY home that CMS lists in Montgomery County falls just inside Fulton County this way; both are NBRC counties.

**Region.** The 63 NBRC counties in Maine, New Hampshire, New York, and Vermont. County shapes are 2024 Census cartographic boundary files (`tigris`, `cb = TRUE`).

**Caveats.** ACS figures are estimates with margins of error, which are widest for the smallest counties (Hamilton County, NY has fewer than 2,000 residents 65+). Beds per 1,000 seniors ignores people crossing county lines for care, so a county with no home may be served by a neighbor.

**Code.** Every number in this dashboard is computed in its source file. Use the `</>` button in the top right to read it.
:::
